In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Tafsir of Surat Ḥā Mīm al-Sajda (Sūrat Fuṣṣilat)

It is Meccan.

His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿Ḥā Mīm﴾. We have already mentioned its meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 2:

As for His saying: ﴿A revelation from the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful﴾, some scholars said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in the verse, as if it were: "A Book, its verses distinguished, is a revelation from the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful." Others said: there is an implied, omitted element in the verse, and the omitted element is "the Qur'an," as if he had said: "The revelation of the Qur'an is from the Most Merciful, the Ever-Merciful." Al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj) said: His saying ﴿revelation﴾ is the subject (mubtada'), and His saying ﴿a Book﴾ is its predicate (khabar).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 3:

And His saying: ﴿Its verses have been detailed﴾. Mujahid said: "They have been explained." Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "They have been detailed with the promise and the threat, and the reward and the punishment." And it is said: "They have been detailed with the lawful and the unlawful."

And His saying: ﴿an Arabic Quran﴾, meaning: in the tongue of the Arabs.

And His saying: ﴿for a people who know﴾, meaning: who reflect upon what is in it out of knowledge.

His saying: ﴿a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾ means: a Qur'an that brings good tidings and warns. So the Qur'an is a bringer of good tidings to the believers and a warner to the disbelievers.

And His saying: ﴿But most of them turn away, so they do not hear﴾ means: they do not listen to the Qur'an.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 5:

And His, the Exalted's, saying: ﴿And they say, "Our hearts are in coverings from that to which you invite us"﴾, meaning: in coverings. Mujahid said: like the quiver for arrows.

And His saying: ﴿And in our ears is deafness﴾, meaning: deafness.

And His saying: ﴿And between us and you is a barrier﴾, meaning: a partition. Some of them said: (A barrier dispersed in the path, a partition in the way). Some of them narrated: that Abu Jahl covered himself with a garment and then said: "O Muhammad, between us and you is a barrier," as mockery. The meaning of the verse is: since they did not listen to the Qur'an with the listening of one who accepts it, they were as though their hearts were in coverings, and in their ears was heaviness and deafness, and between him and them was a barrier.

And His saying: ﴿So act, indeed we are acting﴾, its meaning: [act] by what [you know] of your religion, indeed we are acting by what we know of our religion, as said al-Farra'. Some of them said: act against our destruction, for we are acting against your destruction. Some of them said: act for your deity, for we are acting for our deity.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 6–7:

His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am but a man like you, to whom it is revealed that your God is but one God. So take the straight path to Him﴾ means: turn towards Him in obedience and worship.

And His saying: ﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾ means: from the polytheism in which you are.

And His saying: ﴿And woe to the polytheists, who do not give zakah﴾ means: they do not regard zakah as obligatory upon them as the Muslims regard it. It is also said: the meaning of "giving" (iytha') is upon its apparent sense, and the disbeliever is punished in the Hereafter for not giving zakah, because they are addressed by the legal obligations (shara'i'). This was mentioned by a group of the scholars. Some of them said: ﴿who do not give zakah﴾ means: they do not do that by which they become purified (azkiya'). Some of them said: ﴿who do not give zakah﴾ means: they do not say, "There is no god but Allah." Ibn 'Abbas said, in a narration from 'Ata', so according to this its meaning is: they do not purify themselves from polytheism by accepting monotheism (tawhid). And from Qatadah, who said: zakah is the natural disposition of Islam (fitrat al-Islam); whoever accepts it is saved, and whoever rejects it is destroyed. As for the view we have stated, that it is zakah itself, this was said by al-Hasan al-Basri and a group.

And His saying: ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verses 9–12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: [They were] Sunday and Monday. If someone says: What is the wisdom in creating it in two days, when He was able to create it in an hour or less than that? We say: He created it in two days to guide His creation to deliberation (ina, patience and carefulness) in actions; and so that it would be further from the supposition of coincidence or of a natural act; and because He is not questioned about His creation, so He creates however He wills.

And His saying: ﴿and you set up rivals to Him﴾, that is: equals, likenesses and partners. Hassan ibn Thabit said:

(Do you satirize him, while you are not a match for him... so your sharing with the good is the ransom)

The people of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: His saying ﴿and you set up rivals to Him﴾ means: you obey other than Him in His acts of disobedience. Some of them said: among that is when a man says: "Were it not for the dog of so-and-so, thieves would have entered my house," and "Were it not for the guidance of so-and-so, I would have perished," and what is similar to that.

And His saying: ﴿That is the Lord of the worlds﴾, that is: the One who performed that act is the Lord of the worlds.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and He placed in it firm mountains﴾, that is: mountains that are firm (rawasi), and He named them rawasi for their stability. In the narrative: when Allah, may He be exalted, created the earth, it began to sway and would not settle, so Allah created the mountains upon it and it became stable; this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿and He placed in it firm mountains above it﴾.

And His saying: ﴿and blessed in it﴾, that is: He increased blessing in it. Blessing (barakah) is benefits. Among its blessings are the trees that grow without planting, the grains that grow without sowing, and everything the children of Adam did not make. In some reports: Allah, may He be exalted, gathered in "the bread" the blessings of the heaven and the earth.

And His saying: ﴿and apportioned in it its sustenance﴾. In the exegesis it is said that its meaning is: wheat for one people, barley for a people, maize for a people, dates for a people, fish for a people, and meat for a people. It is said: the Egyptian [food] for Egypt, the Sabiri for Sabir, the Arab [food] for the Arabs, and every food in its place.

And His saying: ﴿in four days﴾, that is: (in the completion of four days). If someone says: Here He said He created the earth in two days, thus mentioning that He began with the creation of the earth; and He said in another place: ﴿And after that He spread the earth﴾ — how then can the two verses be reconciled? The answer: the meaning of His saying ﴿And after that He spread the earth﴾ is: "along with that". This is weak in the language. The more correct view is that the meaning of His saying ("And after that He spread the earth") is: He spread it out. Allah had created the earth before the heavens in two days, and created in it the provisions and sustenance, caused the rivers to flow, made the trees appear, and created the seas in two other days; that makes a completion of four days. The spreading of the earth and making it such that people could dwell in it had not yet happened; when He created the heavens, He spread the earth and made it such that people could inhabit it.

And His saying: ﴿alike for those who ask﴾, that is: equitably for those who ask. Its meaning: whoever asks you about this, answer him with this, for it is the truth and the justice.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾, that is: He intended the creation of the heaven while it was smoke. In the narrative: Allah, may He be exalted, first created water in turmoil; the water foamed into froth, and smoke rose from the froth; He created the earth from the froth and created the heaven from the smoke.

And His saying: ﴿So He said to it and to the earth: Come both, willingly or unwillingly﴾. Some said: the meaning of His saying ﴿come﴾ is: be as I have determined you, willingly or unwillingly; and on this view this speech would be before the creation. The second view, which is that of the majority, is that this speech from Allah, may He be exalted, was after He had created them; according to this, the meaning of "come both, willingly or unwillingly" is: give obedience in what they were created for, compelled or by choice.

And His saying: ﴿They said: We come willingly﴾. Some said: all of this is in the manner of metaphor and not in the manner of literal reality; as if Allah, when He carried out their affairs according to His will and decree, made that equivalent to a speech from Him and a response from them in obedience. The Arabs do mention "said" in such a context. The poet said:

(The pool became full and said: "Enough, enough, I have already filled my belly.")

Some others said: the speech and response are in the literal sense; He placed in the heavens and the earth that by which they understood His address, and they answered in obedience; and this is the preferable view. It is reported from Ibn al-Sammak in his admonition: Ask the earth: Who planted your trees? Who made your rivers flow? Who brought forth your fruits? If it does not answer you by choice, it will answer you by reflection. If it is said: why did He say ﴿obedient﴾ and the grammatical rule would have been "obedient (feminine)"? We say: He said ﴿obedient﴾ (masculine plural) because, when He made them like one who understands in address with them, and their reply, He described the speech in the manner of those who have intellect.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He completed them as seven heavens﴾, that is: He created them as seven heavens ﴿in two days﴾, and these are Thursday and [the] Friday. In some reports: "Allah, may He be exalted, created the earth on Sunday and Monday, created what is disliked on Tuesday, created the sustenance and the trees on Wednesday, created the heavens on Thursday, created in them the constellations, the stars, the sun and the moon on Friday, and created Adam in the last hour of Friday, in haste." The final phrase has been related from Ibn 'Abbas.

And His saying: ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾, that is: He decreed in each heaven its affair. It is said: He created in each heaven what He willed to create in it, including its inhabitants and other things.

And His saying: ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾, that is: with the stars.

And His saying: ﴿and as protection﴾, that is: We protected the heaven with the stars from the devil.

And His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾: its meaning is apparent, and the interpretation of this verse from another aspect will be mentioned as transmitted in the tafsir works.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in He who created the earth in two days﴾ refers to Sunday and Monday, and two is the even number, for it is more than the one, which has nothing below it, and it has not reached three, which is a plural. It is also said: He created it in two days so that it would be a lesson for the angels in looking at His creation more, so that it would be more indicative of His oneness.

As for His saying: ﴿and you set up rivals to Him; that is the Lord of the worlds﴾, we have already explained it.

As for His saying: ﴿and He placed in it firm mountains above it﴾, it is related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: He created the mountains on Tuesday, and He created the heaven, the trees, the seas and the rivers on Wednesday.

As for His saying: ﴿and blessed in it﴾, that is: He increased good in it.

As for His saying: ﴿and apportioned in it its sustenance﴾: in the exegesis, He placed in every land what is not in another, so that people might live together and trade in them, carrying goods from one land to another. It is said: "the Yemeni [item] from Yemen, the Qawhi from Qawhistan, the Sabri from Sabur, the qaratis from Egypt, the Marwi from Marw, the Baghdadi from Baghdad, and the Harawi from Herat." It is related from Mujahid that he said: His saying ﴿apportioned in it its sustenance﴾ is the rain.

As for His saying: ﴿in four days﴾, that is: in the completion of four days. If it is said: two days were mentioned in the first verse and four in this verse, and two more after, so would Allah have created the heavens and the earth in eight days? We say: No, rather He created them in six days.

As for His saying: ﴿in four days﴾, that is: in the completion of four days together with the first two days. This is like a man who says: "I went from Basra to Baghdad in ten days, and I went from Baghdad to Kufa in fifteen days," that is: in the completion of fifteen days along with the first stage. This is the speech of the Arabs, and whoever criticises it has not understood the speech of the Arabs.

As for His saying: ﴿alike for those who ask﴾, we have already explained one of the two meanings; the other meaning is: and apportioned in it its sustenance in four days for those who ask, that is, those in need of food.

As for His saying: ﴿alike﴾, it refers to the days, that is: equal, complete. It is also said: (possessors of) equality. It has been read in the genitive: "alike for those who ask." And it is said: "istawa sawa" according to the first reading.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Then He turned to the heaven while it was smoke﴾: in the exegesis, the smoke was from the breathing of the water. It is said that He first created one heaven, then split it and made it seven heavens, which we have mentioned before.

His saying: ﴿So He said to it and to the earth: Come both, willingly or unwillingly﴾. Some said: it is in the manner of metaphor, like the saying of the poet:

(And the two eyes said to him: "Hearing and obedience," and the two warnings were like pearls when pierced.)

The Arabs say: "The wall said, and so it leaned."

His saying: ﴿Come willingly or unwillingly﴾, that is: respond willingly, otherwise I will compel you to respond unwillingly. They mentioned this meaning only because a command is only directed at an act that is done willingly. Some said: Allah created in the heavens discernment and intellect, so He addressed them and they answered in the literal sense, as we have mentioned. Some said: the address is to those in the heavens and the earth. In the tafsir of al-Naqqash: the place from which the earth answered is al-Urdunn; and also in it: Allah created seventeen kinds of earth, of which this one you see is the smallest of all, and He settled those earths with a people who are neither humans, nor jinn, nor angels. And Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿They said: We come obedient﴾, and He did not say "obedient (dual feminine)". They said: because what is intended is the heavens with those in them, and the earth with those in it. It is also said: because the heavens are seven and the earths are seven; this is related from al-Hasan al-Basri concerning the earth: he said "obedient" because of this number.

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾, that is: He created them. In the exegesis: Allah created the heavens on Thursday, and created the sun, moon, stars, angels and Adam on Friday, and Friday was named Jumu'ah because creation was gathered (ijtama'a) in it. In some exegeses: Allah created Adam in the last hour of Friday and left him for forty years, looking at him and praising Himself, saying: ﴿Blessed is Allah, Lord of the worlds﴾. In some other exegeses too: when Allah created the earth He said to it: "Bring forth your trees, your rivers, and your fruits," and it brought them forth; and when Allah created the heaven He said to it: "Bring forth your sun, your moon, and your stars," and it brought them forth.

His saying: ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾, that is: what sets it right. It is said: He placed in it its inhabitants from the angels.

His saying: ﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps and as protection﴾: we have explained it.

His saying: ﴿and as protection﴾, that is: We protected it from the devils by meteors and stars.

His saying: ﴿That is the decree of the Almighty, the All-Knowing﴾, that is: the decree of the Mighty over what He wills to create, the All-Knowing of His creation and what sets them right.

His statement: ﴿in days of ill omen﴾. It was also read as "nuḥsāt" with the ḥā' vowelled with a sukūn, meaning: ill-omened. These days were ill-omened for them because they were punished during them.

His statement: ﴿that We might make them taste the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world﴾, meaning: a punishment that would disgrace them and humiliate them.

His statement: ﴿And the punishment of the Hereafter is more disgracing﴾, meaning: more intense in disgracing. ﴿And they will not be helped﴾, meaning: they will not be protected from Our punishment.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 17:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And as for Thamud, We guided them﴾. He related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Guided them" means: We showed them the way to guidance. Mujahid said: We made clear to them the path of guidance. It was also said: the path of good and evil. And in some tafsirs: "Guided them" means: We called them.

And His saying: ﴿but they preferred blindness over guidance﴾, meaning: they chose the way of misguidance over the way of rectitude.

And His saying: ﴿So the thunderbolt of the punishment of humiliation seized them﴾. As for "the thunderbolt of the punishment" (ṣāʿiqat al-ʿadhāb): it is a fire that descended from the sky to the earth and struck whoever deserved the punishment.

And His saying: ﴿al-hawn﴾, meaning: the punishment of humiliation (dhī al-hawn). Al-hawn and al-hawān have the same meaning, and it is a punishment that humiliates them and destroys them.

And His saying: ﴿because of what they used to earn﴾, the meaning is apparent.
And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We saved those who believed and used to be mindful of God﴾. That is: they used to guard themselves against shirk (associating partners with God).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 19:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And on the Day when the enemies of Allah are gathered to the Fire, they will be marshaled in order﴾. That is: their first ones are held back until their last ones (catch up).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 20:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Until, when they reach it, their hearing, their sight, and their skins will testify against them as to what they used to do﴾. Most of the exegetes say that the "skins" here are the private parts (al-furuj). In some reports: "Allah, exalted is He, will gather the servants with their mouths sealed (bi-l-fidam), and the first of a person's limbs to speak will be his thigh and his palm."

It has also been said that His saying ﴿and their skins﴾ refers to the well-known skins. In the well-known report transmitted through Anas: "The Prophet (ﷺ) once laughed, and he was asked, 'What made you laugh?' He said: 'I marvel at the servant's disputing with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says: "O Lord, did You not promise me that You would not wrong me?" He says: "Yes." The servant says: "Then I do not accept today any witness against me except from myself." So Allah seals his mouth, and his limbs speak of what he did. The servant then says: "Away with you, and woe! It was on your behalf that I was contending."'"

**"And they will say to their skins, 'Why did you testify against us?' They will say, 'We were made to speak by Allah, who made everything speak.'"** Meaning: everything that speaks.

**"He is the One who created you the first time, and to Him you will be returned."** Meaning: you will be brought back.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 22:

The Most High's saying: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves lest your hearing and your sight and your skins should testify against you﴾. In the well-known reports from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "I was hidden behind the curtain of the Ka'bah, when two Qurashis and a Thaqafi came, or two Thaqafis and a Qurashi, few in understanding of heart and abundant in fat of belly. Some of them said to others: 'Does Allah hear what we say?' One of them said: 'He hears if we speak aloud, and does not hear if we conceal it.' So Allah the Most High revealed: ﴿And you did not conceal yourselves﴾," meaning: you did not hide yourselves (tastakhfun).

His saying: ﴿lest it testify against you﴾ means: from the fear that your hearing, your sight and your skins would testify against you.

His saying: ﴿But you thought that Allah does not know much of what you do﴾ is the statement of one who said: "Indeed Allah hears if we speak aloud, and does not hear if we conceal it."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 23:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿That is your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has ruined you﴾ means what we have said.

And His saying: ﴿it has ruined you﴾ means: it has destroyed you. It is established that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "... I am as My servant thinks of Me, and I am with him when he remembers Me ...".

And in some hadiths: "Allah, exalted is He, commands a servant of His servants to the Fire, and he says: 'My Lord, this was not my assumption of You.' He says: 'And what was your assumption of Me?' The servant says: 'My assumption was that You would forgive me and admit me into Paradise.' So Allah forgives him."

And in some tafsirs: when the servant assumes good, he does good, and when he assumes evil, he does evil.

And His saying: ﴿so you became among the losers﴾ means: among the perished.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 24:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Whether they endure patiently, the Fire is their abode﴾. Al-mathwa (abode): al-manzil (the dwelling place).

And His words: ﴿And if they ask to be shown favour, they will not be among those shown favour﴾. Al-isti'tab (seeking to be shown favour) is the seeking of i'tab (pleasing again), and i'tab is that a person returns to what he loves after having done what displeases it. The Arabs say: "Asta'tabtu fulanan fa-a'tabani" (I asked so-and-so to be pleased with me, and he became pleased with me), with the meaning we have stated.

And His words: ﴿So they will not be among those shown favour﴾: that is, He will not bring them back to what they used to love. It has also been said that what they loved was that He return them to the world so that they would worship Allah and obey Him.

As for His words: ﴿Whether they endure patiently﴾, its meaning is: whether they endure patiently or do not endure patiently. Its meaning is: neither patience nor complaint will benefit them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 25:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And We appointed for them companions﴾, meaning: We made them (into) companions for them. It is also said: We caused them to be (their) companions.

And His saying: ﴿companions﴾, meaning: the devils.

And His saying: ﴿who made fair to them﴾, meaning: the devils made fair to them.

﴿That which was before them﴾, meaning: they made fair to them that there is no resurrection, no Paradise, and no Fire.

And His saying: ﴿and that which was behind them﴾, meaning: they made fair to them the pleasures of the world, and they made fair to them the gathering and hoarding of wealth and its withholding from spending in the way of good.

And His saying: ﴿and the word has been justified against them﴾, meaning: the word became binding upon them ﴿among nations﴾, meaning: along with nations.

And His saying: ﴿who passed away before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers﴾, meaning: they were destroyed, for whoever is destroyed has lost his own self.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 26:

And His statement, the Exalted: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it,"﴾ Al-laghw (vain, idle talk) is every speech that has no sound meaning and no sense underlying it. It has also been said: everything that is not given any attention is laghw. It is said: al-laghw here refers to the whistling and clapping that the polytheists used to do upon hearing the Qur'an, namely al-muka' (whistling) and al-tasdiyah (clapping). We have mentioned this before. In the irregular reading (shadh), it is recited as "wa-lghaw fihi" with a damma on the ghayn, and it has the same meaning as the first. It has also been said that its meaning is: make a clamor upon hearing the Qur'an with noise (al-laghw), namely uproar and shouting, so that you will not be heard.

And His statement: ﴿so that you may overcome﴾, meaning: that you may overcome Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Sam'ani's commentary on the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿So We will surely make those who disbelieve taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them for the worst of what they used to do﴾. He means: the recompense for their evil deeds.

The Most High said: ﴿That is the recompense of the enemies of Allah: the Fire; for them therein is the abode of eternity﴾, meaning: the abode of everlasting dwelling.

The Most High said: ﴿a recompense for their denying Our signs﴾, meaning: they deny them.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 29:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And those who disbelieved will say, "Our Lord, show us those who misled us of the jinn and mankind"﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: The one from among the jinn is Iblis, and the one from among mankind is Qabil (Cain), who killed Habil (Abel). They are the first to establish sin (sanna al-ma'siyah, "to originate a precedent") among the jinn and mankind. This is the well-known view, and it is related from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, which al-Azhari mentioned with his chain of transmission. There is another view regarding the verse: that what is meant is every caller to misguidance among the jinn and mankind. And in some reports: no one from among the jinn who does evil fails to curse Iblis at his death, and no one from among mankind who does evil fails to curse the son of Adam at his death, namely Qabil. It is also said: every doer of evil curses both of them, because they are the two who initiated evil and sins.

As for His words: ﴿that we may put them beneath our feet﴾, meaning: that we may put them beneath our feet in the Fire, which is the lowest level. They said this out of resentment toward them and a desire for vengeance against them.

As for His words: ﴿that they may be among the lowest﴾, meaning: lower than us in the Fire and more severe than us in punishment.

As for His words: ﴿Our Lord, show us﴾, it has been said that its meaning is "give us," and it has been said that the meaning of ﴿show us﴾ is "point them out to us," and this is the preferred view. It is related from al-Suddi that he said: No disbeliever enters the Fire without cursing Iblis, because he was the first to establish disbelief, and no disobedient person enters the Fire without cursing Qabil, because he was the first to establish disobedience.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 30:

The saying of God Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾. It is related from Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Remained steadfast" means they did not associate anything with Allah. And it is related from Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "They did not swerve like the swerving of foxes." It is well known that istiqamah (steadfastness) is obedience to Allah, performing His obligations, and following the Sunnah of His Prophet Muhammad.

﴿...Allah, and then remain steadfast, the angels descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, and rejoice in the Garden which you were promised"﴾.

Thabit related from Anas that the Prophet recited the saying of God Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast﴾, and then said: "Some people said it but did not remain steadfast upon it. Whoever says it and dies upon it has remained steadfast."

And it is related from Sufyan ibn Abdullah al-Thaqafi that he said: "I said, 'O Messenger of Allah, tell me in Islam a saying to which I may hold fast.' He said to him: 'Say, "My Lord is Allah," and then be steadfast.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you fear most for me?' He said: 'This,' and he pointed to his tongue."

It is also well known that the Prophet said: "Be steadfast, and you will not be able to count [your good deeds]; and none maintains ablution except a believer."

His saying: ﴿the angels descend upon them﴾ means at the time of death, and it is said: at the time of resurrection. In the exegesis: when the servant is raised, the two angels who used to guard him and record upon him meet him and say to him: "Do not fear and do not grieve, and rejoice in the Garden which you were promised, and let not what you see terrify you, for it is intended for someone other than you." It is related from Abu al-Aliyah al-Riyahi that he said: "The believer is given glad tidings at three stations: at the entry into the grave, at the resurrection, and at his entry into the Garden."

His saying: ﴿Do not fear﴾ means: do not fear what is before you.

His saying: ﴿and do not grieve﴾ means over what you have left behind of family, children, and property.

His saying: ﴿and rejoice in the Garden which you were promised﴾ means: which you were promised in the books of Allah and upon the tongues of His messengers.

﴿For you therein is whatever your souls desire, and for you therein is whatever you ask, as a welcome from the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful. And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah and does righteous deeds﴾

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 31:

His saying: ﴿We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter﴾. The meaning of wilaya (allyship, guardianship) is: protection, support, and assistance.

His saying: ﴿in the life of this world﴾ means: at the time of death.

﴿And in the Hereafter﴾ means: after the resurrection.

His saying: ﴿And for you therein is what your souls desire﴾ means: what your souls find delight in. It is also said: what occurs to your hearts.

His saying: ﴿And for you therein is what you call for﴾ means: what you wish for. The Arabs say: "Ud'u 'ala ma shi'ta" (ask for whatever you wish), meaning: wish for whatever you want.

It is also said: (And for you therein is what you call for) means: whatever you claim for yourselves, that is yours.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 32:

And His saying: ﴿An provision from the Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾, meaning: a gift from the Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful. From this comes the word nuzl (نزل), meaning the guest's provision (al-dayf), i.e., his gift. It is also said: it means "a gift" (mann).

﴿From the Oft-Forgiving, Most Merciful﴾: al-Ghafur (the Oft-Forgiving) is the One who covers (al-satir), and al-Rahim (the Most Merciful) is the Compassionate (al-'atuf).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 33:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is better in speech than one who invites to Allah and does righteous work and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: "The one who invites to Allah is the Messenger." It is also related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "'Invites to Allah' is general, covering everyone who invites to Allah." And it is related from Mujahid that he said: the verse refers to the muezzins (mu'adhdhinun, those who call the adhan). This view is also related from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her. Some have weakened this view, because the surah is Meccan, and the adhan was legislated after the Hijra to Madina.

As for His words, ﴿and does righteous work﴾, it means: work that is between him and his Lord. It is also said: he does righteous work by performing the obligatory duties (fara'id). And it is said: he does righteous work by sincerity in the invitation and in action.

As for His words, ﴿and says, "Indeed, I am of the Muslims"﴾, it means: he affirms Islam and remains steadfast upon it. It is also said: "of those who submit to the judgment of Allah." It is well known from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, that what is meant by His words ﴿and does righteous work﴾ is the two rak'ahs between the adhan and the iqama. This is according to the view we mentioned: that it was revealed concerning the muezzins.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 34:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And good and evil are not equal﴾. Its meaning: good and evil are not equal, and "lā" is superfluous (ṣila).

As for "good" (al-ḥasana) and "evil" (al-sayyi'a), there are several opinions concerning them:

The first: they are monotheism (tawḥīd) and polytheism (shirk). The second: they are pardon (al-ʿafw) and retaliation (al-intiṣār). The third: they are gentleness in dealing (al-mudārāh) and harshness (al-ghilẓa). The fourth: they are patience (al-ṣabr) and impatience (al-jaza'). The fifth: they are forbearance (al-ḥilm) at the time of anger and foolishness (al-safah).

His saying: ﴿Repel with that which is better﴾. That is: repel the evil with the characteristic which is better. The characteristic which is better is forbearance at the time of anger, pardon at the time of power, patience at the time of trial, and what is similar to that.

There is another opinion regarding the verse: that the meaning of His saying ﴿Repel with that which is better﴾ is: with greeting (al-salām). This was said by Mujāhid. Its meaning is that one greets the one who harms him and does not respond to him with harm. And from Ibn ʿAbbās: the meaning of His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Repel with that which is better﴾ is that if a person harms you, insults you, and attributes to you something ugly, you say to him: "If you are truthful, may God forgive me; and if you are lying, may God forgive you."

His saying: ﴿Then indeed the one between you and him is enmity﴾. This refers to forbearance at the time of anger and pardon at the time of power.

His saying: ﴿As if he were a close friend﴾. That is: a near friend. So the walī (close friend) is the ṣadīq (friend), and the ḥamīm (intimate) is the close relative (qarīb).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 35:

The words of the Most High: ﴿But none is granted it except those who are patient﴾, meaning: none is granted this quality, which is repelling evil with good, except those who are patient, that is, who are patient in obeying the commands of God.

And His words: ﴿But none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾, meaning: one who has a abundant share of religion. It is also said: "None is granted it," meaning: none is granted Paradise except one of great fortune, that is, abundant share. It was said: "One of great fortune," and al-jadd is al-bakht (good fortune).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 36:

The words of Allah Most High: ﴿And if an evil prompting from Satan should incite you, then seek refuge in Allah﴾. That is: anger. And in some reports: "Anger is an ember in the human being, into which Satan blows." And it is said: nazgh means waswasa (whispering).

And His words: ﴿seek refuge in Allah﴾. That is: take refuge (i'tasama) in Allah. We have also related that the Prophet (ﷺ) used to say: "I seek refuge in Allah from Satan, from his hamz, his nafth and his nafkh."

And His words: ﴿Indeed, He is the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing﴾. Its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 37:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And among His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon.﴾ The verse about the night and the day refers to their lengthening and shortening, and the verse about the sun and the moon refers to their revolving according to a known reckoning.

And His saying: ﴿Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon.﴾ ʿIkrimah said: the sun is like the world and a third of it, and the moon is like the world once. And one of them reported: the sun's length is eighty farsakhs and its width sixty farsakhs. And God knows best.

And His saying: ﴿But prostrate to God, who created them, if it is Him that you worship.﴾ That is: that you single Him out (tawhid) in worship.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 38:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿But if they are arrogant﴾, meaning: they show arrogance (takabbaru).

And His saying: ﴿those who are near your Lord﴾, meaning: the angels.

﴿They glorify Him night and day, and they never tire﴾, meaning: they do not become bored. It is related from Ka'b al-Ahbar (Ka'b al-Ahbar, the Jewish convert to Islam and transmitter of Israelite narratives) that he said: The glorification (tasbih) of the angels is like the breath and the blink of the eye for the children of Adam. Just as no weariness reaches a human being through the blink of the eye and the breath, so too no weariness reaches them through glorifying (Allah).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 39:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And among His signs is that you see the earth humbled﴾, meaning: dry, crushed, dead, with nothing upon it.

And His words: ﴿But when We send down water upon it, it stirs﴾, meaning: it moves for the sake of vegetation.

And His words: ﴿and swells﴾, meaning: the vegetation rises up. And the second opinion is that this is by inversion (al-taqdim wa'l-ta'khir, transposition of words), and its meaning is: "it swells and stirs," that is, the earth swells with the emergence of plants from it, and "stirs" means it moves.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, He who revived it﴾, meaning: He who revived the dead earth, ﴿is the Reviver of the dead﴾, meaning: on the Day of Resurrection.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, He is Powerful over all things﴾, meaning: Able.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 40:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our verses﴾ means: they incline toward denial (al-juhud) and [rejection] concerning Our verses. Everyone who inclines from the truth to falsehood, and from monotheism (tawhid) to polytheism (shirk), is a deviator (mulhid).

And His saying: ﴿are not hidden from Us﴾ means: their disbelief is not hidden from Us.

His saying: ﴿Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ On this there are several opinions. The first: the one thrown into the Fire is Abu Jahl, and the one who comes secure is ʿAmmar. This is related by ʿIkrimah and others.

The second opinion: the one thrown into the Fire is Abu Jahl, and the one who comes secure is Hamzah ibn ʿAbd al-Muttalib.

The third opinion: the one thrown into the Fire is every disbeliever, and the one who comes secure is the Messenger (ﷺ). It is also said: every believer has been made secure from abiding in the Fire. It is also said: those thrown into the Fire are those who hate the family of the Prophet (ﷺ), and those who come secure are those who love them. It was also said: this refers to the Companions. And Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿Do what you will﴾ is in the manner of threat and warning. Its meaning: do what you will, for you will be brought before it.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾ is clear in meaning.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder (al-dhikr) when it comes to them﴾. That is, in the Qur'an. There is an ellipsis (hadhf) in the verse, and the omitted element is: they will be recompensed for that.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed it is a Book Mighty (ʿazīz)﴾. That is, noble with Allah. It is also said: a Book that Allah has made mighty (aʿazzahu Allah).

"And His saying: ﴿No falsehood comes to it from before it or behind it﴾ — there are two opinions concerning it. The first: falsehood does not come to it, meaning that no denial comes to it from the earlier scriptures, and no book comes after it to abrogate (naskh) and supersede it. The second opinion: the falsehood is Iblis, may the curse be upon him, and the meaning is that he does not come to it with any addition or any subtraction; that is, he has no authority over it in either of these respects.

And His saying: ﴿A revelation from One who is All-Wise, Most Praiseworthy﴾ — that is, Wise in His actions, Praiseworthy in His words."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 43:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you.﴾ This is by way of consolation and solace for the Prophet, for the disbelievers used to say: he is a disbeliever, a sorcerer, a poet, and a madman. So God, may He be exalted, consoling and comforting him, said: ﴿Nothing is said to you except what was said to the messengers before you.﴾ That is: you are not the first to whom this has been said, for the prophets before you were attributed these things. The discourse on this is complete. Then He said: ﴿Indeed your Lord is possessor of forgiveness﴾, that is, for the sins of the servants, for whomever He wills to forgive.

His statement: ﴿and possessor of painful punishment﴾, that is, for whomever He wills not to forgive.

Regarding His statement: ﴿Falsehood does not come to it from before it or from behind it﴾ there is another opinion: its meaning is that falsehood does not come to it before its complete descent, so "from before it" [means that].

His statement: ﴿from before it﴾, that is, before the revelation, for the messengers gave good news of the Qur'an, so there does not come to it anything that refutes or nullifies it. ﴿Nor from behind it﴾, that is, after the revelation, and its meaning is: no book comes to it that abrogates it (naskh).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 44:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And had We made it a non-Arabic Qur'an﴾, meaning: in the tongue of the non-Arabs (ʿajam). It is also said: "a non-Arabic (aʿjamiyyan)" means: unclear (ghayr mubin), as related by al-Mufaddal, but the first (interpretation) is the well-known one.

And His saying: ﴿they would have said, "Why were its verses not explained in detail?" — "Is it a non-Arabic (Qur'an) and an Arab (Messenger)?"﴾ Its meaning: "Is it a non-Arabic Qur'an and an Arab Messenger?"

Ibn ʿAbbas and al-Hasan recited: "Lawla fussilat ayatuhu ʿajamiyyun wa ʿarabiyyun" not in the form of a question, meaning: "Why was it not made that some of its verses are non-Arabic and some of its verses are Arabic?" The preferred reading is the first, according to the first meaning. Al-aʿjamiyy (the non-Arabic-speaker, one with a speech impediment or foreign tongue) is everyone in whose tongue there is ʿujma (non-Arabic inflection or impediment), even if he is an Arab; from this comes the expression "the non-Arab poet" (ziyadat al-aʿjamiyy al-shaʿir). Al-ʿajamiyy is the individual from the ʿajam (non-Arabs), al-aʿrabiyy is everyone who dwells in the desert, and al-ʿarabiyy is the individual from the ʿArab. The poet said:

(And I have not seen one like me whose heart was stirred by a sound like hers, nor an Arab stirred by a non-Arabic sound.)

It is said: the verse was revealed concerning Yasar, the slave of Ibn al-Hadrami, who used to enter upon the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He was a Jew who had read the scriptures. They said: "Yasar, Abu Fukayha, teaches Muhammad." Abu Fukayha said: "No, rather I learn from him, and he teaches me."

And His saying: ﴿Say: It is, for those who believe, a guidance and a healing﴾, meaning: the Qur'an is guidance for the eyes (absar) and healing for the hearts.

And His saying: ﴿And as for those who do not believe, in their ears is deafness﴾, meaning: heaviness and deafness, as though He placed them in the station of the deaf, since they did not hear with the hearing of one who accepts.

And His saying: ﴿and it is for them a blindness﴾. Al-Farra' said: they were blind and deaf to the Qur'an, in that they did not benefit from it. It was also said: their eyesight was blinded to the Qur'an, so the Qur'an for them is in the position of blindness.

And His saying: ﴿Those are called from a place far away﴾, meaning: far from their hearts. This is related from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib (raḍiya Allahu ʿanhu). It is also said: "called from a far place" means: the sky. Al-Farra' said: the Arabs say of one who does not understand speech that "he is taking it from a far place," and when he understands they say "he is taking it from a near place."

Some grammarians mentioned that His saying, ﴿Those are called from a place far away﴾, is the response (jawab) to His saying, ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder when it comes to them﴾. What we have mentioned, that the response is omitted, is the more preferable, and we have explained it. Related by al-Nahhas.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 45:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book, but differences arose concerning it﴾. The Book is the Torah (al-Tawrah), and the disagreement concerning it is that some of them believed in it and some of them disbelieved in it.

And His saying: ﴿And had it not been for a word that preceded from your Lord﴾, meaning: the delay of the Resurrection until a term known to Him. It is narrated from ʿAṭāʾ, who said: The word that preceded from His Lord is that when Adam, upon him be peace, sneezed, God, exalted is He, inspired him until he said: "All praise is due to God." So God, exalted is He, said: "May your Lord have mercy upon you." That is the word that preceded from God.

And His saying: ﴿it would have been decided between them﴾, meaning: the punishment would have been hastened for them.

And His saying: ﴿And indeed, they are in disquieting doubt about it﴾, meaning: in doubt (murtab).

"And His saying: ﴿Whoever does righteousness, it is for his own self﴾, meaning: the benefit of that returns to himself.

And His saying: ﴿And whoever does evil, it is against it﴾, meaning: the harm of that returns upon him.

And His saying: ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾, because what He does is justice, and it cannot be injustice. It is also said: the meaning of His saying ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾ is: He does not punish anyone without a crime."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿To Him is referred the knowledge of the Hour﴾. Its meaning: to God is returned the knowledge of the Hour. This is general, for everyone who is asked about the Hour says: "God knows best."

His saying: ﴿And no fruit comes out of its sheaths﴾ means: out of their containers and coverings. The kumm (sheath) is its covering. It is also said that it is the sheath of the spathe (jufr al-tal').

His saying: ﴿Nor does any female conceive or give birth except with His knowledge﴾ means: He knows the duration of the pregnancy and He knows the time of its delivery.

His saying: ﴿And on the Day He will call them﴾ means: He will call out to the disbelievers, ﴿"Where are My partners?"﴾ according to your claim?

In the tafsir it is related that God, may He be exalted, says: "Where are the kings? Where are the tyrants? Where are the gods? I am the Lord, there is no lord besides Me. I am God, there is no god besides Me. I am the King, there is no king besides Me."

His saying: ﴿They will say, "We have informed You"﴾ means: we have made You aware (a'lamnaka). From this derive the words adhn (notification), adhan (call to prayer) and mu'adhdhin (caller to prayer). This is the speech of the gods.

Al-Farra' and others said: its meaning is that the gods say: "We have informed You, O Lord, of their denial and their disbelief," ﴿"None of us bears witness"﴾, meaning: none of us testifies that their claim is true and their assertion is correct.

And His words: ﴿And what they used to invoke before has vanished from them﴾, meaning: it became void for them and escaped them, ﴿what they used to invoke before﴾.

And His words: ﴿And they will realize that they have no place of refuge﴾, meaning: they became certain that they have no shelter or place of escape.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 49:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Man does not tire of asking for good⁠﴾, i.e., of asking for wealth. It is also said: it means wealth after poverty and health after sickness. It was also said that the verse was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, who would never stop asking for abundant wealth, and concerning him the words of Him, may He be exalted, were revealed: ﴿And I made for him abundant wealth and sons present [with him]⁠﴾.

His saying: ﴿But when evil touches him⁠﴾, i.e., affliction, poverty and hardship.

His saying: ﴿Then he is despairing and hopeless⁠﴾, i.e., despairing of good, hopeless of mercy. It was also said: qunut (hopelessness) means having a bad opinion of his Lord, as if he were saying: Allah, may He be exalted, will not remove from me this affliction and hardship.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 50:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We give him a mercy from Us after some adversity has touched him﴾ means: ease after hardship, and wealth after poverty.

And His saying: ﴿he will surely say, "This is mine"﴾ means: by my own effort and my deservingness.

And His saying: ﴿And I do not think the Hour will be established﴾ means: coming.

And His saying: ﴿And if I am returned to my Lord﴾ means: brought back.

And His saying: ﴿indeed, I will have with Him the best [reward]﴾ means: much good.

Some scholars said: The disbeliever is between two false wishes, in this world and in the Hereafter. As for in this world, he says: "And if I am returned to my Lord, indeed I will have with Him the best [reward]." And as for in the Hereafter, he says when he sees what his hands have sent forward: "Would that I had been dust." In the tafsir of al-Naqqash it is reported that the verse was revealed concerning ʿUqbah ibn Rabiʿah, Shaybah ibn Rabiʿah, al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah, Ubayy ibn Khalaf, Umayyah ibn Khalaf and others, and they used to entertain themselves with falsehoods.

And His saying: ﴿Then We will surely inform those who disbelieved of what they did﴾ is in the manner of threat and warning.

And His saying: ﴿and We will surely make them taste a severe punishment﴾ means: harsh.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 51:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And when We bestow favour upon man, he turns away and withdraws to his side﴾. It is also read: "wa-nā bi-janibihi" (and he moves away on his side). The meaning of "nā'in bi-janibihi" is that he distances himself to his side.

And His words: ﴿And when evil touches him﴾, that is, hardship and affliction.

And His words: ﴿then he has abundant supplication﴾, that is, much. Al-Naqqash said: the verse refers to those whose mention preceded. It is reported from some of the scholars ('ulama') that he said: "There is a servant who knows God in ease but does not know Him in hardship, and there is a servant who knows God in hardship but does not know Him in ease. The believer is the one who knows Him in both ease and hardship."

And in the well-known report, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Guard God and He will guard you. Guard God and you will find Him before you. Become known to God in ease and He will know you in hardship. When you ask, ask God, and when you seek help, seek help from God..." The report continues to its end.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 52:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Say: "Have you considered? If it is from Allah, and you disbelieve in it..."﴾ mean: Say, O disbelievers, "Have you considered: if it is from Allah?" That is, the Qur'an.

And His words: ﴿then you disbelieve in it﴾ mean: in the Qur'an.

And His words: ﴿Who is more astray than one who is in extreme dissension?﴾ mean: in great opposition to the truth. The meaning is: you, O disbelievers, are in dissension and error.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 53:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿We shall show them Our signs in the horizons and within themselves﴾. The signs in the horizons are the signs of the heavens and the earths: that is, the raising of the sky, the creation of the stars, the revolving of the sphere, the shining of the sun and the moon, and what is similar to that. Likewise the spreading out of the earth, the setting up of the mountains, the gushing forth of the rivers, and the planting of trees, and so on without end.

As for His words, ﴿and within themselves﴾, that is: [the signs in] hearing and sight, and the creation of all the limbs and all the senses. In some tafsir works it is said: among the signs within the self is that food and drink enter from one place and exit from two places. It was also said: the entry of foods of many kinds and their exit as one kind. Al-Suddi said: the signs in the horizons are the conquests of the cities, and the signs within themselves are the conquest of Mecca by the Messenger. It is also said: the signs in the horizons are the conquests that took place after the Messenger, and the signs within themselves are those that took place in the time of the Messenger. It was also said: the signs in the horizons are what was reported of the earlier nations and what befell them, and the signs within themselves are what He warned them of in terms of threat and punishment. Mujahid said: the signs in the horizons are the withholding of rain from the sky, and the signs within themselves are the afflictions in the bodies.

As for His words, ﴿until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth﴾, meaning: that the Messenger is the truth. It was also said: the Qur'an is the truth.

As for His words, ﴿Is it not sufficient concerning your Lord﴾, meaning: Is it not sufficient for you, O Muhammad, from your Lord [that] He is over all things a witness? It was also said its meaning is: Is there not sufficiency in the testimony of your Lord? It was also said: Is there not sufficiency in the proof which He established for monotheism?

As for His words, ﴿that He is over all things a witness﴾, that is: because He is over all things a witness, or [it is sufficient] that He is over all things a witness.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 41, verse 54:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Surely they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord.﴾ That is: in doubt about the resurrection and the rising up (from the graves).

And His saying: ﴿Surely He encompasses all things.﴾ That is: His knowledge encompasses all of that. The surah is complete.
